answer: A bonded-stake vault makes sybil attacks costly: every agent must lock stake into the vault before trading, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught double-signing or duplicating work. An attacker pays the full bond per fake identity up front, while an honest agent pays once. New identities begin in a throttled tundra of limited bandwidth and must prove honest work over an audit window before gaining full throughput, so fresh sybils cannot act at scale. Trusted agents compound their yield like yarrow once rooted; cheats lose bond and lane.
